scenarioStory.history: Working near a propane tank on a rural property when it ruptured and ignited, engulfing her in flame for approximately 8-10 seconds before a coworker smothered the fire with a blanket. Denies loss of consciousness, denies being in an enclosed space or confined structure. No hoarseness, stridor, soot in the mouth or nares, or singed nasal/facial hair noted.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 44-year-old female with extensive partial and full-thickness thermal burns to the torso and bilateral thighs following a propane flash fire. She is alert and in severe pain, with no evidence of airway involvement. → TBSA calculated, fluids initiated: Crew estimates TBSA at 50% using the Rule of 9's, calculates the Rule of 10 initial fluid rate, establishes IV access through unburned skin, covers the burns with a dry dressing, and manages pain. → Fluid rate titrated on reassessment: Fluid rate is titrated based on reassessment, the patient is kept warm to prevent heat loss from her large area of skin loss, and she is transported directly to the regional burn center with ongoing pain management.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Severe burns to torso and bilateral thighs after a propane tank flash fire

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 44-year-old female with extensive partial and full-thickness thermal burns to the torso and bilateral thighs following a propane flash fire. She is alert and in severe pain, with no evidence of airway involvement.

scenarioEvents.name: TBSA calculated, fluids initiated
scenarioEvents.description: Crew estimates TBSA at 50% using the Rule of 9's, calculates the Rule of 10 initial fluid rate, establishes IV access through unburned skin, covers the burns with a dry dressing, and manages pain.
relatedChecklist: Estimate TBSA at 50% using Rule of 9's; exclude first-degree burns from the calculation
Establish IV access through unburned skin, avoiding burned areas
Initiate LR or NS at 500 mL/hr (50% TBSA x 10 mL/hr/%TBSA, Rule of 10, patient 68 kg within 40-80 kg range)
Cover burns with dry dressing or clean sheet; do not apply gels or ointments
Fentanyl 68 mcg IV (68 kg x 1 mcg/kg; max initial dose 100 mcg)

scenarioEvents.name: Fluid rate titrated on reassessment
scenarioEvents.description: Fluid rate is titrated based on reassessment, the patient is kept warm to prevent heat loss from her large area of skin loss, and she is transported directly to the regional burn center with ongoing pain management.
relatedChecklist: Prevent systemic heat loss; keep patient warm with blankets
Transport directly to a burn center (TBSA greater than 10% with torso involvement)

scenarioEvents.name: TBSA rounded incorrectly, rate under-dosed
scenarioEvents.description: The crew underestimates or rounds down the TBSA, resulting in an under-calculated fluid rate. Without adequate volume replacement, the patient trends toward hypovolemic shock despite the large burn surface area.
relatedChecklist: Recalculate TBSA and fluid rate; correct infusion up to 500 mL/hr
